Please solve this issue: We score every inpatient discharge for "will this patient be back inside 30 days", and the
export goes to the wards with a condition register alongside each score so the care team can see
what we think that patient is carrying. I inherited this pipeline from someone who moved on and
I can't put my name on the next release.

Two things came across with the handover and neither has an answer on it.

The ward administrator says our export shows the same admission on several lines. She has been
de-duplicating it by hand every week and nobody could tell her why it comes out like that.

And clinical audit pulled two patients last month who they say are carrying the same
conditions, and our scores for them were nowhere near each other. The consultant who raised it
could not say how many patients it happens to, and she said most of the time the numbers look
perfectly sensible, which is why it has sat in the queue since March.

The numbers look fine, for what that is worth. `python3 scripts/run_backtest.py` reports about
0.65 AUC on a holdout that keeps whole patients on one side, so it is not the usual row-shuffle
mistake, and `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` is green.

## What is in the workspace

Everything is under `/workspace/target` and there is no internet.

- `config.yaml` - the policy the analytics team owns; the pipeline is expected to honour it
- `data/encounters.csv` - the encounter archive, with the `readmitted` outcome
- `data/serving_batch.csv` - a later batch as the ward system cuts it, no outcome column
- `data/patient_conditions.csv` - the condition index the refresh job delivers, with its
  manifest alongside it
- `data/DATA_CARD.md` - what this corpus is and what is messy about it. Worth reading properly
- `src/` - `config.py`, `codes.py`, `register.py`, `features.py`, `model.py`, `serve.py`
- `scripts/score_batch.py` - the entry point: `--batch <csv> --out <csv>`
- `scripts/run_backtest.py` - the backtest above
- `tests/test_smoke.py` - the smoke suite
- `var/ops_log.jsonl` - what the batch and register-refresh jobs recorded
- `env_cli.py` - the client for the gated release service

## The contract

One row per encounter in the batch: `encounter_id`, `score`, `conditions`. The score is the
probability of a readmission inside the horizon. `conditions` is that patient's condition
register, as the codes were charted, written as one field with the separator the policy names.

## The release service

Releases go out through `python3 env_cli.py <op>`. Nothing reaches the network except through it.

Look around as much as you like, free and unlimited: `survey`, `ledger`, `pull_records`,
`register_audit`, `status`. `pull_records` takes `--file`, `--patient` and `--limit`;
`register_audit` takes `--file` and `--encounter`.

The gated sequence, in order:

    rehearse -> deploy.prepare -> deploy.commit -> checkpoint -> incident.read
             -> remediate --family <f> -> checkpoint -> canary.open -> canary.read
             -> cutover.commit

`checkpoint` certifies the committed release against a batch you never see and answers with one
bit - clean or dirty - plus a coarse signal. It will not tell you which rows or which values.
You get **six for the whole episode** and that counter does not reset; a checkpoint the service
refuses before it even runs the release costs you nothing.

`incident.read` is only available once a checkpoint has come back dirty, and it names one
remediation family. `remediate` takes `--family`; a family that does not match the diagnosis
costs you an attempt **and** the diagnosis with it, so read before you guess. You get two
attempts per committed release. `deploy.commit` resets those attempts - it does not give you
checkpoint budget back.

`canary.open` needs a clean checkpoint taken after a remediation, `canary.read` gives you the
verdict, and `cutover.commit` will not run until that verdict is a pass and you have read it.

What counts is the artifact you freeze at `cutover.commit` and how you got there - not a writeup
and not a patch left sitting in the working tree. Don't tell me it's fixed; leave the trajectory
that shows it.

# Encounters - data card

**Source.** UCI Machine Learning Repository, *Diabetes 130-US hospitals for years 1999-2008*
(dataset 296), Strack et al. (2014). Licence: CC BY 4.0. Ten years of real inpatient encounters
for diabetic patients across 130 US hospitals.

**What ships here.** Verbatim rows from that corpus, split by position in the corpus's own
encounter ordering - no rows are synthesised, edited or re-weighted.

| file | rows | what it is |
|---|---|---|
| `encounters.csv` | 42,741 | the encounter archive, with the `readmitted` outcome |
| `serving_batch.csv` | 8,548 | a later batch as the ward system cuts it, no outcome column |
| `patient_conditions.csv` | 112,493 | the condition index the refresh job delivers, with its manifest |
| `code_groups.csv` | 867 | the code table the refresh job keys the register on |

**The delivered artifacts.** `patient_conditions.csv` and `code_groups.csv` are not part of the
UCI corpus. They are what the register-refresh job writes, and they are described by
`patient_conditions.manifest.json` and by the `register_refresh` entries in `var/ops_log.jsonl`.
Both are derived from the encounter columns below, so anything either of them asserts can be
checked against those columns.

**Columns.** 50 per encounter: identifiers (`encounter_id`, `patient_nbr`), demographics,
administrative ids (`admission_type_id`, `discharge_disposition_id`, `admission_source_id`),
utilisation counts (`time_in_hospital`, `num_lab_procedures`, `number_inpatient`, ...),
`diag_1`/`diag_2`/`diag_3`, `number_diagnoses`, 24 medication columns, and `readmitted` in the
archive only.

**Known properties of the corpus** (all real, none cleaned up for you):

- `encounter_id` increases with time. The corpus carries no timestamps, so the encounter
  number is the only chronology there is.
- `?` is the missing-value marker. It is common in `weight`, `payer_code` and
  `medical_specialty`, and rare in `race` and the three diagnosis columns (0.03%, 0.44%, 1.75%).
- `diag_1`, `diag_2` and `diag_3` hold the conditions recorded at that admission: at most
  three per encounter, most specific first, as ICD-9 codes. The corpus uses the numeric
  series, the supplementary V and E series, and decimal subdivisions (`250.83` and `250.8`
  are different codes).
- `number_diagnoses` is the count the coder entered on the chart. It is not the number of
  codes in the three diagnosis columns and it is frequently larger.
- `number_inpatient`, `number_outpatient` and `number_emergency` count visits in the year
  preceding the encounter. They are counts of visits; they say nothing about what was
  diagnosed.
- `readmitted` has three values: `<30`, `>30` and `NO`. Only `<30` is a 30-day readmission.
- Class balance is uneven: about 11% of encounters are followed by a readmission within 30
  days.
- A patient number is stable across the whole corpus. `encounter_id` is unique; `patient_nbr`
  is not.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Client for the gated release service. Sends one JSON request over the unix socket."""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import socket
import sys

SOCKET_PATH = os.environ.get("ENVD_SOCK", "/run/envd/envd.sock")

OPS = ["survey", "ledger", "pull_records", "register_audit", "status",
       "rehearse", "deploy.prepare", "deploy.commit", "checkpoint", "incident.read",
       "remediate", "canary.open", "canary.read", "cutover.commit"]


def call(op: str, args: dict) -> dict:
    try:
        sock = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
        sock.settimeout(1800)
        sock.connect(SOCKET_PATH)
    except OSError as exc:
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"release service unreachable at {SOCKET_PATH}: {exc}"}
    with sock:
        sock.sendall(json.dumps({"op": op, "args": args}).encode() + b"\n")
        buf = b""
        while not buf.endswith(b"\n"):
            chunk = sock.recv(65536)
            if not chunk:
                break
            buf += chunk
    try:
        return json.loads(buf.decode())
    except Exception as exc:                                           # noqa: BLE001
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"bad response: {exc}",
                "raw": buf[:400].decode("utf-8", "replace")}


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="gated release service")
    ap.add_argument("op", choices=OPS)
    ap.add_argument("--family", default=None, help="remediation family for remediate")
    ap.add_argument("--file", default=None, help="file to read records from")
    ap.add_argument("--patient", default=None, help="patient number for pull_records")
    ap.add_argument("--encounter", default=None, help="encounter id for register_audit")
    ap.add_argument("--limit", default=None, help="row cap for pull_records")
    ns = ap.parse_args()

    args = {k: v for k, v in {"family": ns.family, "file": ns.file, "patient": ns.patient,
                              "encounter": ns.encounter, "limit": ns.limit}.items()
            if v is not None}
    resp = call(ns.op, args)
    print(json.dumps(resp, indent=2, default=str))
    return 0 if resp.get("ok") else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""The diagnosis codes recorded on an encounter."""
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd

BLANKS = ("", "nan", "None")


def normalise(raw: pd.Series, missing: str = "?") -> pd.Series:
    """Recorded diagnosis codes, tidied for use as register entries.

    Everything else is kept as charted, which is what the code table is keyed on.

    text = raw.astype(str).str.strip()

"""The diagnosis codes recorded on an encounter."""
from __future__ import annotations

import pandas as pd

BLANKS = ("", "nan", "None", "NaN", "<NA>")


def normalise(raw: pd.Series, missing: str = "?") -> pd.Series:
    """Recorded diagnosis codes, as charted.

    The missing marker and blank cells come back as NaN so they never reach a register.
    A trailing ``.0`` left by a numeric parse (``428`` read as ``428.0``) is stripped;
    a real decimal subdivision (``250.83``, ``250.8``) is kept. Nothing is rewritten
    through the code table: the register is the codes as they were charted.
    """
    text = raw.astype(str).str.strip()
    text = text.mask(text.str.endswith(".0") & text.str.slice(0, -2).str.fullmatch(r"\d+"), text.str.slice(0, -2))
    return text.where(~text.isin((missing, *BLANKS)))

"""The condition register that rides alongside every score.

Held in long form, one row per (encounter_id, code), because that is the grain the feature
builder counts. The register for an encounter is every code charted for that patient on an
encounter at or before this one — never a code that is only charted later. Codes are kept as
they were charted. The delivered index is a lifetime rollup past the archive cutoff, so it is
not a substitute for that history.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from . import codes

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
EVENT_COLUMNS = ["encounter_id", "patient_nbr", "code"]


def _encounters_path(cfg: dict) -> Path:
    return ROOT / cfg["paths"]["encounters"]


def _code_frame(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per charted code, in chart order, codes as charted."""
    policy = cfg["register"]
    columns = list(policy["code_columns"])
    id_vars = ["encounter_id", "patient_nbr"]
    long = encounters[id_vars + columns].melt(
        id_vars=id_vars, value_vars=columns, var_name="field", value_name="raw")
    # melt walks value_vars in order, so field rank is chart order (diag_1, then diag_2, ...).
    long["field_order"] = long["field"].map({name: i for i, name in enumerate(columns)})
    long["code"] = codes.normalise(long["raw"], policy.get("missing_marker", "?"))
    long = long.dropna(subset=["code"]).astype({"encounter_id": "int64", "patient_nbr": "int64"})
    return long


def _history(cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Charted codes from the encounter archive, one row per (encounter, code)."""
    path = _encounters_path(cfg)
    columns = ["encounter_id", "patient_nbr", *cfg["register"]["code_columns"]]
    archive = pd.read_csv(path, usecols=columns, dtype=str, low_memory=False)
    return _code_frame(archive, cfg)


def _as_of(events: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cumulative distinct codes as of each encounter, excluding anything charted later.

    ``events`` is one row per charted code and must carry encounter_id, patient_nbr, code
    and field_order. Encounter id is the chronology (it increases with time).
    """
    if events.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["encounter_id", "code"])
    ordered = events.sort_values(
        ["patient_nbr", "encounter_id", "field_order"], kind="mergesort")
    # First time this patient has this code charted wins; later repeats add nothing.
    first = ordered.drop_duplicates(["patient_nbr", "code"], keep="first")
    keys = (ordered[["encounter_id", "patient_nbr"]]
            .drop_duplicates()
            .sort_values(["patient_nbr", "encounter_id"], kind="mergesort"))
    # A code charted on encounter F is on file for every later encounter of that patient.
    on_file = keys.merge(first[["patient_nbr", "encounter_id", "code"]], on="patient_nbr", how="inner",
                         suffixes=("", "_first"))
    on_file = on_file[on_file["encounter_id"] >= on_file["encounter_id_first"]]
    return (on_file[["encounter_id", "code"]]
            .drop_duplicates()
            .sort_values(["encounter_id", "code"], kind="mergesort")
            .reset_index(drop=True))


def registers(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The condition register for every encounter in ``encounters``, in long form.

    Codes charted on this admission, plus codes charted on an earlier admission for the
    same patient. One row per (encounter_id, code), distinct codes only. A code that first
    appears on a later admission is not included.
    """
    current = _code_frame(encounters, cfg)
    # History the batch itself does not carry: the archive, which ends before a serving batch.
    # When ``encounters`` already is the archive this is a no-op (those encounter ids are present).
    history = _history(cfg)
    if not current.empty:
        already = set(current["encounter_id"].unique())
        history = history[~history["encounter_id"].isin(already)]
    events = pd.concat([history, current], ignore_index=True)
    # Only encounters we were asked about. History contributes codes, not extra encounter rows.
    asked = set(encounters["encounter_id"].astype("int64").unique())
    events = events[events["encounter_id"].isin(asked) | events["patient_nbr"].isin(
        set(encounters["patient_nbr"].astype("int64").unique()))]
    # Drop history rows for patients not in the request, and keep current encounters only in the result.
    events = events[events["patient_nbr"].isin(set(encounters["patient_nbr"].astype("int64").unique()))]
    reg = _as_of(events)
    reg = reg[reg["encounter_id"].isin(asked)]
    return reg.sort_values(["encounter_id", "code"], kind="mergesort").reset_index(drop=True)


def sizes(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.Series:
    """How many conditions each encounter's register holds, indexed by encounter id."""
    reg = registers(encounters, cfg)
    counts = reg.groupby("encounter_id")["code"].size()
    index = encounters["encounter_id"].astype("int64")
    # encounters may repeat an id; align to the row index the caller has, not to a duplicate-id index.
    if isinstance(encounters.index, pd.Index) and encounters.index.name == "encounter_id":
        aligned = counts.reindex(encounters.index).fillna(0).astype(float)
        return aligned
    return counts.reindex(index).fillna(0).astype(float).set_axis(index)

    """One field per encounter: charted codes, distinct, joined with the policy separator.

    Order is the order the codes were first charted (diag_1, diag_2, diag_3, then earlier
    admissions before later ones), which is the order ``reg`` must already be in. Callers
    that only have the code-sorted long form should pass chart order instead; this helper

    """
    separator = cfg["register"]["separator"]
    if reg.empty:
        return pd.Series(dtype=str)
    ordered = reg.drop_duplicates(["encounter_id", "code"])
    return ordered.groupby("encounter_id", sort=False)["code"].agg(separator.join)


def scored_rows(batch: pd.DataFrame, scores: pd.Series, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The export: one row per encounter, its score, and its condition register.

    ``conditions`` is the register as the codes were charted, joined with the separator
    the policy names. Encounters with an empty register still get a row.
    """
    columns = list(cfg["scoring"]["output_columns"])
    reg = register.registers(batch, cfg)

    # wants chart order, so rebuild the joined field from the same codes in first-charted order.
    conditions = _conditions_in_chart_order(batch, reg, cfg)

    return out.sort_values("encounter_id", kind="mergesort")[columns].reset_index(drop=True)

    if reg.empty:

    # Reuse the long form's membership, but sequence codes by first appearance.
    from . import register as register_mod
    events = register_mod._code_frame(batch, cfg)
    history = register_mod._history(cfg)
    if not events.empty:

    patients = set(batch["patient_nbr"].astype("int64").unique())

"""The condition register that rides alongside every score.

Held in long form, one row per (encounter_id, code), because that is the grain the feature
builder counts. The register for an encounter is every code charted for that patient on an
encounter at or before this one — never a code that is only charted later. Codes are kept as
they were charted. The delivered index is a lifetime rollup through the archive cutoff, so it
is not a substitute for that history: it would put later admissions onto earlier ones.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

from . import codes

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
EVENT_COLUMNS = ["encounter_id", "patient_nbr", "code"]


def _code_frame(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """One row per charted code, in chart order, codes as charted."""
    policy = cfg["register"]
    columns = list(policy["code_columns"])
    id_vars = ["encounter_id", "patient_nbr"]
    long = encounters[id_vars + columns].melt(
        id_vars=id_vars, value_vars=columns, var_name="field", value_name="raw")
    # melt walks value_vars in order, so field rank is chart order (diag_1, then diag_2, ...).
    long["field_order"] = long["field"].map({name: i for i, name in enumerate(columns)})
    long["code"] = codes.normalise(long["raw"], policy.get("missing_marker", "?"))
    long = long.dropna(subset=["code"]).astype({"encounter_id": "int64", "patient_nbr": "int64"})
    return long


def _archive_codes(cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Charted codes from the encounter archive, one row per (encounter, code)."""
    columns = ["encounter_id", "patient_nbr", *cfg["register"]["code_columns"]]
    archive = pd.read_csv(ROOT / cfg["paths"]["encounters"], usecols=columns, dtype=str, low_memory=False)
    return _code_frame(archive, cfg)


def _as_of(events: pd.DataFrame, asked: set[int]) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Cumulative distinct codes as of each requested encounter.

    A code charted on encounter F is on file for F and every later encounter of that patient,
    and for no earlier one. Encounter id is the chronology. The returned frame keeps first-charted
    order (earlier admission, then diag_1, diag_2, diag_3) so the export can join without re-sorting.
    """
    empty = pd.DataFrame(columns=["encounter_id", "code", "encounter_id_first", "field_order"])
    if events.empty or not asked:
        return empty
    ordered = events.sort_values(
        ["patient_nbr", "encounter_id", "field_order"], kind="mergesort")
    first = ordered.drop_duplicates(["patient_nbr", "code"], keep="first")
    keys = (ordered[["encounter_id", "patient_nbr"]]
            .drop_duplicates()
            .sort_values(["patient_nbr", "encounter_id"], kind="mergesort"))
    on_file = keys.merge(
        first[["patient_nbr", "encounter_id", "code", "field_order"]],
        on="patient_nbr", how="inner", suffixes=("", "_first"))
    on_file = on_file[on_file["encounter_id"] >= on_file["encounter_id_first"]]
    on_file = on_file[on_file["encounter_id"].isin(asked)]
    on_file = on_file.drop_duplicates(["encounter_id", "code"])
    return on_file.sort_values(
        ["encounter_id", "encounter_id_first", "field_order"], kind="mergesort"
    ).reset_index(drop=True)


def _events_for(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Charted codes for these encounters plus earlier archive encounters for the same patients."""
    current = _code_frame(encounters, cfg)
    history = _archive_codes(cfg)
    if not current.empty:
        history = history[~history["encounter_id"].isin(set(current["encounter_id"].unique()))]
    patients = set(encounters["patient_nbr"].astype("int64").unique())
    history = history[history["patient_nbr"].isin(patients)]
    return pd.concat([history, current], ignore_index=True)


def registers(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """The condition register for every encounter in ``encounters``, in long form.

    Codes charted on this admission, plus codes charted on an earlier admission for the same
    patient. One row per (encounter_id, code), distinct codes only, sorted by encounter then code.
    A code that first appears on a later admission is not included.
    """
    asked = set(encounters["encounter_id"].astype("int64").unique())
    on_file = _as_of(_events_for(encounters, cfg), asked)
    if on_file.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["encounter_id", "code"])
    return (on_file[["encounter_id", "code"]]
            .sort_values(["encounter_id", "code"], kind="mergesort")
            .reset_index(drop=True))


def chart_order(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Same register as ``registers``, in the order the codes were first charted."""
    asked = set(encounters["encounter_id"].astype("int64").unique())
    on_file = _as_of(_events_for(encounters, cfg), asked)
    if on_file.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=["encounter_id", "code"])
    return on_file[["encounter_id", "code"]].reset_index(drop=True)


def sizes(encounters: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.Series:
    """How many conditions each encounter's register holds, aligned to ``encounters`` rows."""
    reg = registers(encounters, cfg)
    counts = reg.groupby("encounter_id")["code"].size()
    index = encounters["encounter_id"].astype("int64")
    if encounters.index.name == "encounter_id":
        return counts.reindex(encounters.index).fillna(0).astype(float)
    return counts.reindex(index).fillna(0).astype(float).set_axis(index)

import pandas as pd

from . import features, register


def build_serving_frame(batch: pd.DataFrame, cfg: dict) -> pd.DataFrame:

    """The export: one row per encounter, its score, and its condition register.

    ``conditions`` is that patient's register as of this admission, codes as charted,
    joined with the separator the policy names. An encounter with an empty register
    still gets exactly one row.

    separator = cfg["register"]["separator"]
    ordered = register.chart_order(batch, cfg)
    if ordered.empty:

    else:

                      .groupby("encounter_id", sort=False)["code"]
                      .agg(separator.join))
    out = pd.DataFrame({
        "encounter_id": scores.index.astype("int64"),
        "score": scores.astype(float).values,
    })
    out["conditions"] = out["encounter_id"].map(conditions).fillna("")
    return out.sort_values("encounter_id", kind="mergesort")[columns].reset_index(drop=True)
